whyThisMatters:
BBCS is the system of record for a blood bank: donors, inventory, patients, and billing. It is FDA-cleared. A mother started it in the 1980s. Her son bought it in 2019 and spent five years moving it to the cloud. Customers are still coming off the old on-prem system.

He says they do not lose customers and they do not lose employees. The banks they serve supply about a fifth of the blood products in the United States. Nearly ten million a year. Forty people. No outside funding. July 2025 interview. Self-reported.

You pay because the blood has to be tracked, and the old system is the one you are leaving slowly.

FDA clearance is the part that makes this a slow sale. Five years of rebuilding, and customers are still on the old system. Forty people and no outside money is the shape he describes. The fifth of US blood products is his claim about the customers, not a market share I measured.
